existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: For each standard 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 black-and-white copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per-page charge of up to 15 cents ($0.15).
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: For each standard 8 1/2" x 11" or 8 1/2" x 14" copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per page charge of up to 15 cents ($0.15) for black and white copies ... If producing duplex (front and back) copies, a charge for two separate pages may be imposed for each single duplex copy.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II.A
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Ceiling (up to $0.15). City sets the operative rate at or below this in its policy; a higher rate requires documented actual-cost analysis (TN-0031). Duplex counts as two pages.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: For each standard 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 color copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per-page charge of up to 50 cents ($0.50).
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: For each standard 8 1/2" x 11" or 8 1/2" x 14" copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per page charge of ... up to 50 cents ($0.50) for color copies.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II.A
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Ceiling. If color is dearer and the record can be produced in B&W, the custodian must advise the requestor it can be produced in B&W unless the requestor will pay the higher color charge (Schedule § II.B).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Actual-cost charges above the schedule with documentation
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: If actual costs are higher than the schedule amounts, or records are produced on a non-standard medium, the entity may develop its own charges but must document 'actual cost' calculation and reasoning in an adopted policy; charges above $0.15 (B&W) / $0.50 (color) require documented actual-cost analysis.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Actual production cost exceeds the schedule amounts, or non-standard medium is used.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: If a governmental entity's actual costs are higher than those reflected above ... the governmental entity may develop its own charges. The governmental entity must establish a schedule of charges documenting "actual cost" and state the calculation and reasoning for its charges in a properly adopted policy. ... Charges greater than 15 cents ($0.15) for black and white copies and 50 cents ($0.50) for color copies can be assessed or collected only when there is documented analysis of the fact that the higher charges represent the governmental entity's actual cost of producing such material, unless there exists another basis in law for such charges.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II.C
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Same concept as the ceiling rows (TN-0029/0030) under a different basis — do not split as a separate rate; this is the escape valve above the guideline ceiling.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: First hour of labor not chargeable (labor threshold)
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The labor threshold is the first (1st) hour of labor reasonably necessary to produce requested material; a governmental entity may adopt a higher threshold, and labor may be charged only for time exceeding the threshold.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: A request for copies requiring labor to locate, retrieve, review, redact, and reproduce records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: "Labor threshold" is the first (1st) hour of labor reasonably necessary to produce requested material(s). A governmental entity may adopt a higher labor threshold than one (1) hour. A records custodian is only permitted to charge for labor exceeding the labor threshold established by the governmental entity.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § IV.C
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Floor: minimum one free hour; city may set a higher (more generous) threshold. Aggregation removes this waiver (TN-0038).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Labor rate = hourly wage of employee(s) reasonably necessary
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Labor above the threshold is charged at the hourly wage of the employee(s) reasonably necessary, using the lowest practicable wage; the hourly wage is the employee's base salary (excluding benefits), computed by dividing annual salary by required hours per year.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Labor time exceeds the labor threshold.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: "Labor" is the time (in hours) reasonably necessary to produce requested records, including the time spent locating, retrieving, reviewing, redacting, and reproducing records. ... "Hourly wage of an employee" is based upon the base salary of the employee and does not include benefits. If an employee is not paid on an hourly basis, the hourly wage shall be determined by dividing the employee's annual salary by the required hours to be worked per year. ... In calculating labor charges, a records custodian should determine the total amount of labor for each employee and subtract the labor threshold from the labor of the highest paid employee(s).
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges §§ IV.B, IV.D, IV.E
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Rate is a computed value keyed to specific employees' wages, not a fixed number; the one free hour is deducted from the highest-paid employee's time.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Itemized cost estimate before producing copies
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The records custodian shall provide the requestor an estimate of the reasonable costs to provide copies of the requested material before producing them.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: A request for copies that will incur charges.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The records custodian shall provide a requestor an estimate of the reasonable costs to provide copies of the requested material.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_authority: Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B); OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.G; OORC Model Public Records Policy § VI.B
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Model Policy § VI.B: 'Records custodians shall provide requestors with an itemized estimate of the charges ... prior to producing copies ... and may require pre-payment.'

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Payment for copies may be required before production
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A records custodian may require payment for copies before producing the copies of the records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A records custodian may require payment for copies before producing copies of the records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.E; Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B)
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Non-payment of estimated fees is itself a permitted denial/hold ground (OORC Response Form). City sets the dollar threshold above which prepayment is required.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Discretionary reduction or waiver of charges
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A records custodian may reduce or waive charges, in whole or in part, in accordance with the governmental entity's public records policy.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Application of the entity's fee-waiver provisions.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A records custodian may reduce or waive charges, in whole or in part, in accordance with the governmental entity's public records policy.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.D
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: City sets waiver thresholds; fees on aggregated requests are typically non-waivable (TN-0038).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Actual cost of storage media, outside vendor, and retrieval
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A custodian may charge actual out-of-pocket cost for flash drives/storage devices provided; if internal production is not practicable, may use an outside vendor and charge those actual costs; and may recover actual retrieval charges assessed by an archive or other entity holding the records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Electronic media supplied, outside-vendor production, or retrieval from an archive/other holder.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A records custodian may charge its actual out-of-pocket costs for flash drives or similar storage devices on which electronic copies are provided. ... If it is not practicable or feasible for the records custodian to produce copies internally, the records custodian may use an outside vendor and charge the costs to the requester. ... If a records custodian is assessed a charge to retrieve requested records from archives or any other entity having possession of requested records, the records custodian may recover from the requestor the costs assessed for retrieval.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges §§ III.B, III.E, III.F
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Actual-cost pass-throughs (basis 'fixed' = the actual amount incurred). Per-page charges for electronic records only when paper had to be produced (e.g., printed to redact).

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity's policy shall specify the number of requests within a calendar month that triggers aggregation; that amount must be no lower than four (4) requests.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Multiple/frequent requests within a calendar month reaching the entity's threshold.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A governmental entity's public record policy shall indicate the number of requests within a calendar month that will trigger aggregation; that amount must be no lower than four (4) requests. This amount is the aggregation threshold.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § I.D
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Floor: statewide minimum threshold is 4/month; the city fills the operative number at or above 4. Once reached, the labor-threshold waiver no longer applies (TN-0039).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Loss of labor-threshold waiver once aggregation threshold met
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Once a records custodian reaches the aggregation threshold, the custodian is no longer required to deduct the labor threshold or any other minimum charge per request that would ordinarily be waived.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Once a records custodian reaches the aggregation threshold, the records custodian is no longer required to deduct the labor threshold set forth in the Schedule of Reasonable Charges or any other minimum charge per request that would ordinarily be waived.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § II.A

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Aggregation across requestors acting in concert
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: An entity may aggregate multiple requests by a single requestor, and may aggregate requests by multiple requestors if the coordinator determines they are acting in concert with each other or as agents of another person, entity, or organization.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Multiple requests by one requestor, or by several requestors the coordinator finds are acting in concert/as agents.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A governmental entity may aggregate multiple public record requests made by a single requestor. A governmental entity may also aggregate public record requests made by multiple requestors, if the public records request coordinator determines the requestors are acting in concert with each other or as the agents of another person, entity, or organization.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § I.C
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: 'Working in concert' is a coordinator determination; it is appealable to the OORC (TN-0041).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Special fees for specific documents requested for a specific use
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Although standard copy/labor charges do not vary by purpose, other statutory provisions (e.g., § 10-7-506(c)) enumerate fees that may be assessed when specific documents are requested for a specific use.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Request for specific enumerated documents for a specific (e.g., commercial) use governed by § 10-7-506(c).
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: However, other statutory provisions, such as Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-506(c), enumerate fees that may be assessed when specific documents are requested for a specific use. Any distinctions made, or waiver of charges permitted, based upon the type of records requested should be expressly set forth and permitted in the adopted public records policy.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.F, citing Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-506(c)
existing_fee_payment_rules.effective_status: Requires manual verification of § 10-7-506(c) enumerated documents/rates
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: The verbatim capture is the OORC Schedule's reference; the specific documents and fee amounts in § 10-7-506(c) were not opened verbatim and need a later pass. Flags human legal review.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Statutory authority to charge reasonable production costs
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A records custodian may require a requestor to pay the custodian's reasonable costs incurred in producing the requested material, assessed in the manner established by the Office of Open Records Counsel pursuant to § 8-4-604.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: A request for copies/production of public records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A records custodian may require a requestor to pay the custodian's reasonable costs incurred in producing the requested material and to assess the reasonable costs in the manner established by the office of open records counsel pursuant to § 8-4-604.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Statutory hook that makes the OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges the operative cost framework. § 10-7-506(a) separately grants custodians the right to adopt and enforce reasonable rules governing the making of copies (per OORC Model Policy, Policy Considerations).
